sections.title: リーディング・ライティング

items.q: After the long flight, Mia felt (　) and fell asleep as soon as she got to the hotel.
items.ex: exhausted で「くたくたに疲れた」。長いフライトのあとすぐ眠ったことに合います。

items.q: The museum has a large (　) of paintings from the 19th century.
items.ex: collection で「収集品、コレクション」。

items.q: The police asked people to (　) from using the road until the fallen trees were removed.
items.ex: refrain from ～ing で「～するのを控える」。

items.q: The two companies decided to (　) and become one large company.
items.ex: merge で「合併する」。emerge は「現れる」です。

items.q: This bridge was built more than 100 years ago, but it is still in good (　).
items.ex: in good condition で「良い状態で」。

items.q: Many students find it hard to (　) on their studies when their phones are nearby.
items.ex: concentrate on ～ で「～に集中する」。

items.q: Learning a new language takes a lot of time and (　), but it is worth it.
items.ex: effort で「努力」。time and effort で「時間と労力」。

items.q: Tom was (　) for being late to the meeting again, so he promised to leave home earlier.
items.ex: criticize A for B で「BのことでAを批判する」。また遅刻したので注意されました。

items.q: The hotel offers a free shuttle bus to the airport, which is very (　) for guests with heavy luggage.
items.ex: convenient で「便利な」。

items.q: Prices at the supermarket have risen (　) this year, so many families are trying to save money.
items.ex: sharply で「急激に」。値上がりしたので節約している、という流れ。

items.q:
A: Can you (　) for me at the meeting tomorrow? I have to see a doctor.
B: Sure, no problem.
items.ex: fill in for ～ で「～の代わりを務める」。

items.q: Sarah's parents were against her plan at first, but she finally (　) them to let her study in Spain.
items.ex: persuade A to do で「Aを説得して～させる」。

items.q: The concert was so popular that all the tickets were sold out (　) minutes.
items.ex: within ～ で「～以内に」。

items.q: The old man insisted on (　) the heavy box by himself, even though his son offered to help.
items.ex: insist on ～ing で「～すると言い張る」。前置詞 on のあとは動名詞。

items.q: (　) the bad weather, the soccer game continued until the end.
items.ex: Despite + 名詞 で「～にもかかわらず」。In spite は of が必要、Although のあとは主語と動詞が続きます。

items.q: If I (　) about the traffic jam, I would have left home earlier.
items.ex: 過去の事実と反対の仮定(仮定法過去完了)は If + had + 過去分詞, would have + 過去分詞。

items.q: It was not until he lost his wallet (　) Ben realized how careless he had been.
items.ex: It was not until A that B で「Aして初めてBした」。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.title: Light Pollution
blocks.body:
For most of human history, people could look up at night and see thousands of stars. Today, however, about 80 percent of the world's population lives under skies that are polluted by artificial light. In large cities, people may only be able to see a few dozen stars ( 18 ).
Light pollution is not just a problem for people who enjoy looking at the stars. It can also ( 19 ). Many animals depend on natural light and darkness. For example, baby sea turtles find their way to the ocean by moving toward the brightest horizon. When bright lights from buildings and roads are near the beach, the turtles often crawl in the wrong direction.
Some towns are now trying to reduce light pollution. They use streetlights that point downward and switch off the lights in empty buildings at night. ( 20 ), these changes help towns save money on electricity.

qs.ex: 都会では「晴れた夜でさえ」数十個の星しか見えない。
直後にウミガメの赤ちゃんが道に迷う例があるので「野生生物に害を与える」。
光害を減らす効果に加えて「さらに」電気代も節約できる、という追加です。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: Living in Tiny Houses
blocks.body:
In recent years, a growing number of people in the United States have chosen to live in "tiny houses." These homes are usually smaller than 40 square meters, and some are built on wheels so that they can be moved. Although they are small, they include everything people need, such as a kitchen, a bathroom, and a sleeping area.
One reason for their popularity is cost. A tiny house costs much less than a regular house, so owners ( 21 ). Many owners also say that living in a small space has changed their lifestyle. Because there is little room for extra things, they ( 22 ) and focus on experiences rather than possessions.
However, tiny houses are not for everyone. Families with children may find them too crowded. Moreover, in some areas, local rules do not allow people to live in such small homes. ( 23 ), owners sometimes have difficulty finding a place to put their houses.

qs.ex: 普通の家よりずっと安いので「大きなローンを避けられる」。

o: buy only what they really need
qs.ex: 余分な物を置く場所がない→「本当に必要な物だけ買う」→物より経験を重視、という流れ。
小さな家に住むことを認めない地域がある→「その結果」家を置く場所を見つけにくい。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Riverside Community Center
To: Photography Workshop Members
Date: April 18
Subject: Changes to the spring workshop

Dear members,
Thank you for signing up for our spring photography workshop. We are writing to let you know about some changes. Unfortunately, our instructor, Mr. Lee, broke his arm last week and will not be able to teach for a while. Fortunately, Ms. Rachel Moore, a professional photographer who has taught at our center before, has agreed to take his place.
Because Ms. Moore is busy on weekends, the workshop will now be held on Wednesday evenings from 7 p.m. to 9 p.m. instead of Saturday mornings. The first class will be on May 6. If you cannot attend on Wednesdays, please contact the front desk by April 30, and you will receive a full refund.
In the final class, each member will choose their three best photos, and they will be displayed in the center's lobby for a month. Please remember to bring your own camera to every class. Smartphones are also fine for the first two classes.
We look forward to seeing you.
Riverside Community Center

qs.q: Why will Mr. Lee not teach the workshop?
o: He has moved to another city.
He decided to work as a professional photographer.
qs.ex: Mr. Lee, broke his arm last week とあります。週末が忙しいのは代わりの Ms. Moore です。

qs.q: What should members do if they cannot come on Wednesdays?
o: Contact the front desk by April 30.
Send an email to Ms. Moore.
Attend only the first two classes.
qs.ex: please contact the front desk by April 30 とあります。

qs.q: What will happen in the final class?
o: Members will choose photos to be displayed.
Ms. Moore will show her own photos.
qs.ex: each member will choose their three best photos, and they will be displayed とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: The Concorde
blocks.body:
On January 21, 1976, two passenger planes took off at the same time, one from London and one from Paris. They were the first commercial flights of the Concorde, a plane that could fly at about twice the speed of sound. A trip from London to New York, which usually takes around seven hours, took only about three and a half hours on the Concorde.
The Concorde was a remarkable achievement of engineering. It was built jointly by the United Kingdom and France, and it flew at a height of about 18,000 meters, much higher than ordinary passenger planes. From their windows, passengers could see the curve of the Earth. However, the plane also had serious problems. When it flew faster than sound, it created a loud noise called a sonic boom. Because of this noise, many countries did not allow it to fly at supersonic speed over land, so it was used mainly for flights across the Atlantic Ocean.
The Concorde was also very expensive to operate. It used a huge amount of fuel and could carry only about 100 passengers, so tickets cost far more than ordinary ones. In 2000, a Concorde crashed shortly after taking off from Paris. Although the planes returned to service the next year, the number of passengers did not recover, and the Concorde made its last flight in 2003.
Today, some companies are trying to develop a new generation of supersonic passenger planes. Engineers are working on designs that would make the sonic boom much quieter, so that the planes could fly fast over land as well. If they succeed, super-fast air travel may become possible again.

qs.q: What was special about the Concorde?
o: It could carry more passengers than any other plane.
It was the first plane to fly across the Atlantic.
It could fly at about twice the speed of sound.
It was built only by France.
qs.ex: a plane that could fly at about twice the speed of sound とあります。英仏の共同開発です。

qs.q: Why was the Concorde used mainly for flights across the Atlantic Ocean?
o: Its loud sonic boom was not allowed over land in many countries.
It could not fly at night.
It needed to refuel in the middle of the ocean.
Passengers wanted to see the curve of the Earth.
qs.ex: ソニックブームのため陸の上での超音速飛行が認められず、大西洋路線が中心でした。

qs.q: What is one reason tickets for the Concorde were so expensive?
o: It flew only once a week.
Its seats were larger than first-class seats.
It used a lot of fuel and carried few passengers.
qs.ex: It used a huge amount of fuel and could carry only about 100 passengers とあります。

qs.q: What happened after the crash in 2000?
o: Fewer passengers chose to fly on it.
It began to fly over land.
qs.ex: 翌年に運航を再開しましたが、乗客の数は戻りませんでした。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: The Concorde flew at the same height as ordinary planes.
The Concorde made its last flight in 2000.
Engineers are trying to make the sonic boom quieter.
The Concorde was built by the United States.
qs.ex: Engineers are working on designs that would make the sonic boom much quieter とあります。最後の飛行は2003年。

parts.prompt:
以下の英文を読んで、その内容を英語で要約し、解答欄に記入しなさい。
語数の目安は45語〜55語です。
parts.body:
These days, many people use smartphone apps to sell things they no longer need, such as clothes, books, and games. Selling an item is easy: users just take a photo of it, write a short description, and set a price. When someone buys it, the seller sends it by mail.
These apps have several benefits. People can earn some money from things that would otherwise be thrown away. Buyers, on the other hand, can get items for much less than the price of new ones. Some people also say that these apps help reduce waste, because used items get a second life.
However, using these apps can cause trouble. Sometimes an item is in worse condition than the seller described, and the buyer and seller argue about it. In addition, packing and sending items takes time and effort, which some sellers find stressful.
rules: 解答は、英文要約の解答欄に書きなさい。なお、解答欄の外に書かれたものは採点されません。
要約の内容が英文から逸れていると判断された場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。英文をよく読んでから答えてください。
parts.model: Many people now use smartphone apps to sell their used items easily. Sellers can earn money, buyers can get things cheaply, and the apps may reduce waste. However, items are sometimes worse than described, causing arguments, and packing and sending items can be stressful for sellers.
checks: 第1段落(不要な物をアプリで簡単に売れる)の内容が入っている
第2段落の利点(お金になる・安く買える・ごみが減る)が入っている
第3段落の問題点(説明と状態がちがうトラブル・発送の手間)が入っている
本文の表現を言いかえて短くまとめている(However などで対比)
語数が45〜55語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英文要約)

parts.prompt:
以下のTOPICについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ書きなさい。
POINTSは理由を書く際の参考となる観点を示したものです。ただし、これら以外の観点から理由を書いてもかまいません。

TOPIC
Some people say that the government should spend more money on space exploration. Do you agree with this opinion?

POINTS
・Science and technology
・Cost
・The future
rules: 語数の目安は80語〜100語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
TOPICに示された問いに答えていない場合や、内容がTOPICからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I agree that the government should spend more money on space exploration. I have two reasons. First, space research leads to new technology that improves our daily lives. For example, satellites help us forecast the weather and use GPS on our smartphones. Second, space exploration inspires young people to study science and engineering. When children see astronauts working in space, they may dream of becoming scientists themselves. For these reasons, I believe investing in space exploration is worthwhile for the future.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
理由を2つ書き、それぞれに具体的な説明がある
POINTSの観点(科学技術・将来など)を使っている
最後に結論をもう一度書いている
語数が80〜100語になっている
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Hi, Dan. Are you going to the company barbecue on Saturday?
I'd like to, but my sister is moving into a new apartment that day, and I promised to help her.
That's too bad. Everyone was hoping you'd bring your famous potato salad.
I could make some on Friday night and ask you to take it.
items.q: What will the man probably do?
o: Go to the barbecue after helping his sister.
Ask his sister to make potato salad.
Make potato salad for the woman to take.
items.ex: 金曜の夜にポテトサラダを作って、女性に持って行ってもらうと言っています。

lines: Excuse me. I booked a twin room for three nights, but your website says I only have two nights.
Let me check, sir. You're right. It seems there was a problem with our system. I'll add the third night now.
Thank you. Will the price be the same?
Yes, and we'll give you free breakfast for the trouble.
items.q: What will the hotel do for the man?
o: Reduce the price of his room.
items.ex: we'll give you free breakfast for the trouble と言っています。料金は同じです。

lines: Mark, have you finished the sales report for the meeting tomorrow?
Almost. I'm still waiting for the numbers from the Osaka office.
They called this morning. They said they'd send them by three.
Great. Then I can finish it before I leave tonight.
items.q: What is the man waiting for?
items.ex: 大阪支社からの数字(データ)を待っています。

lines: Honey, our refrigerator isn't keeping things cold anymore.
Is it broken? It's only five years old.
I think so. Should we buy a new one?
Let's ask a repair person to look at it first. If it can't be fixed, then we'll buy one.
OK. I'll call the repair shop tomorrow.
items.q: What does the woman suggest?
items.ex: まず修理の人に見てもらい、直らなければ買う、と提案しています。

lines: Excuse me, I'd like to return these shoes. They hurt my feet.
Only once, for about an hour.
I'm sorry, but we can't accept returns of shoes that have been worn outside. However, we can stretch them a little for you.
items.q: What will the man do?
o: Make the shoes a little bigger.
Give the woman her money back.
Exchange the shoes for another pair.
items.ex: stretch them(くつを伸ばして少し大きくする)ことになりました。返品はできません。

lines: Did you hear that the city is going to close the public pool next year?
The building is old, and repairing it would cost too much. They're planning to build a new sports center instead, but it won't open for three years.
That's a long time. I guess I'll have to join a private gym.
items.q: Why will the pool be closed?
o: A private gym will open nearby.
It would be too expensive to repair.
The city needs the land for a park.
items.ex: repairing it would cost too much と言っています。

lines: Hello, I'm calling about the part-time job at your café. Is it still available?
Yes, it is. Have you worked at a café before?
Yes, for two years when I was in college.
Great. Could you come in for an interview on Thursday afternoon?
items.q: What will the woman do on Thursday?
items.ex: 木曜日の午後2時に面接を受けます。

lines: Hi, Lisa. You look really tanned. Did you go somewhere?
Yes, I spent a week in Hawaii with my family.
Lucky you! Did you go surfing?
I tried, but I kept falling off the board. I spent most of the time snorkeling instead.
items.q: What did Lisa do most of the time in Hawaii?
items.ex: I spent most of the time snorkeling instead. と言っています。サーフィンはうまくいきませんでした。

lines: Professor Clark, could I have a few more days to finish my essay?
The deadline is Friday. What's the problem?
I've been sick with the flu all week, and I couldn't do much research.
I see. Then you can hand it in next Wednesday. But please bring a note from your doctor.
items.q: What does the professor ask the student to do?
o: Bring a note from her doctor.
items.ex: please bring a note from your doctor と言っています。しめ切りは来週の水曜日に延びました。

lines: Emma, are you going to take the train to the conference in Fukuoka?
I was planning to, but it takes about five hours. I'm thinking of flying instead.
Flights are expensive this week, though, because of the holiday.
Hmm. Maybe I'll take the night bus. It's cheap, and I can sleep on the way.
items.q: How will Emma probably go to Fukuoka?
items.ex: 飛行機は高いので、安くて寝ながら行ける夜行バスにしそうです。

lines: Hi, I ordered a sofa from your online store two weeks ago, but it hasn't arrived yet.
I'm very sorry. Could you tell me your order number?
Thank you. It looks like the sofa is still at our warehouse. We'll deliver it this Saturday.
OK. Please make sure it comes in the morning.
items.q: Why is the woman calling?
o: Her sofa has not been delivered.
She wants to cancel her order.
She wants to change her address.
items.ex: 2週間前に注文したソファがまだ届いていないからです。

lines: Mom, I'm thinking of quitting the tennis club.
Why? You've been playing for three years.
I want to spend more time studying for my university entrance exams.
I understand, but exercise is important, too. Why don't you talk to your coach about practicing fewer days a week?
items.q: What does the mother suggest?
o: Quitting the tennis club right away.
Talking to the coach about practicing less.
items.ex: 練習の日数を減らせないかコーチに相談するよう勧めています。

lines: Excuse me, does this train stop at Shin-Yokohama?
No, this is a rapid train. It doesn't stop there.
Oh no. I need to get there by ten.
Get off at the next station and change to a local train. You should still make it in time.
items.q: What does the man tell the woman to do?
o: Change trains at the next station.
items.ex: 次の駅で降りて各駅停車に乗りかえるよう言っています。

lines: Have you decided what to do for your summer vacation?
I'm going to volunteer at an animal shelter in my hometown.
That sounds rewarding. What will you do there?
Mainly walk the dogs and help clean the cages. I also want to help find new owners for the animals.
items.q: Where will the woman spend her summer vacation?
items.ex: volunteer at an animal shelter(動物保護施設)と言っています。

lines: The printer on our floor is broken again.
Again? I called the repair company last week.
No, I think it's time to buy a new one. I'll talk to the manager about it this afternoon.
items.q: What will the man do this afternoon?
o: Use the printer on another floor.
items.ex: I'll talk to the manager about it this afternoon. と言っています。

lines: Akira works as an air traffic controller at a busy airport. His job is to give instructions to pilots so that planes can take off and land safely. Because he must stay focused, he takes a break every two hours. He says the hardest part of his job is bad weather, when many flights are delayed at the same time.
items.q: What does Akira say is the hardest part of his job?
items.ex: the hardest part of his job is bad weather とあります。

lines: Attention, passengers. Due to an accident near Central Station, all trains on the Green Line have stopped. We expect service to restart in about thirty minutes. Passengers who are in a hurry can use the free shuttle buses from the north exit.
items.q: What can passengers in a hurry do?
o: Get a refund at the ticket office.
items.ex: Passengers who are in a hurry can use the free shuttle buses とあります。

lines: The Great Wall of China was built over many centuries to protect the country from invaders. Contrary to a popular belief, it cannot easily be seen from space with the naked eye. Although the wall is very long, it is quite narrow, and its color is similar to the land around it.
items.q: Why is it hard to see the Great Wall from space?
o: Most of it has been destroyed.
It is narrow and similar in color to the land.
It is always covered by clouds.
items.ex: it is quite narrow, and its color is similar to the land around it とあります。

lines: Last year, Rina started a small online shop selling handmade earrings. At first, she had only a few customers. Then she began posting videos of how she makes the earrings on social media. The videos became popular, and now she gets more orders than she can make by herself.
items.q: How did Rina get more customers?
items.ex: 作り方の動画をSNSに投稿して人気が出ました。

lines: Welcome to Hilltop Botanical Garden. This month, our rose garden is in full bloom. Please stay on the paths and do not pick any flowers. Free guided walks start every hour from the information desk near the main gate.
items.q: Where do the free guided walks start?
items.ex: Free guided walks start every hour from the information desk とあります。

lines: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backward. Their wings move so fast, up to 80 times per second, that they make a humming sound. Because flying uses so much energy, hummingbirds must eat almost all day long, visiting hundreds of flowers to drink nectar.
items.q: Why do hummingbirds eat almost all day?
o: Flying uses a lot of energy.
items.ex: Because flying uses so much energy とあります。

lines: Daisuke had always wanted to visit Europe, but he was afraid of flying. To get over his fear, he joined a special course offered by an airline. Pilots explained how planes work and why turbulence is not dangerous. Last month, Daisuke finally flew to Italy, and he even enjoyed the flight.
items.q: How did Daisuke get over his fear of flying?
o: He joined a course offered by an airline.
He took medicine before the flight.
He asked a friend to go with him.
items.ex: he joined a special course offered by an airline とあります。

lines: Thank you for shopping at Brightway Electronics. This weekend only, all laptops are 15 percent off. Customers who buy a laptop will also receive a free mouse. Our store will be open until 10 p.m. on both Saturday and Sunday.
items.q: What will customers who buy a laptop receive?
items.ex: Customers who buy a laptop will also receive a free mouse. とあります。割引は15%です。

lines: Many people think that bats are blind. In fact, all bats can see, and some large bats have very good eyesight. However, many small bats mainly use sound to find their way in the dark. They make high-pitched sounds and listen for the echoes.
items.q: How do many small bats find their way in the dark?
items.ex: 高い音を出して、そのはね返り(echoes)を聞いて進みます。

lines: Every summer, Yuto's town holds a dragon boat race on the river. Teams of twenty people row together to the beat of a drum. This year, Yuto's team practiced every evening for two months. Although they did not win, they finished in third place, their best result ever.
items.q: How did Yuto's team do in the race this year?
items.ex: they finished in third place, their best result ever とあります。

lines: Good morning, students. This Friday, the school will hold a fire drill during third period. When you hear the alarm, follow your teacher's instructions and walk, do not run, to the schoolyard. Please do not talk during the drill.
items.q: What should students do when they hear the alarm?
items.ex: follow your teacher's instructions とあります。走らず歩いて校庭へ。

lines: When Hannah moved to Japan to teach English, she could not use chopsticks well. Her students offered to help her practice during lunch. They taught her to pick up small things such as beans. After a few months, she could use chopsticks better than some of her students.
items.q: Who helped Hannah practice using chopsticks?
items.ex: Her students offered to help her practice during lunch. とあります。

lines: In the Netherlands, there are more bicycles than people. Many roads have special lanes for bikes, and some cities have huge parking areas that can hold thousands of bicycles. Because the country is very flat, cycling is an easy way to get around.
items.q: Why is cycling easy in the Netherlands?
items.ex: Because the country is very flat とあります。

lines: Mr. Tanaka runs a small bakery. Recently, the price of flour has gone up, so he had to decide whether to raise the price of his bread. Instead, he started selling smaller loaves at the same price. He says his regular customers understand the situation.
items.q: What did Mr. Tanaka decide to do?
o: Raise the price of his bread.
Sell smaller loaves at the same price.
items.ex: he started selling smaller loaves at the same price とあります。

lines: Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Sky Tower. The observation deck is on the 50th floor. On clear days, you can see the mountains to the west. Please note that the elevator to the observation deck will stop running at 9:30 p.m., thirty minutes before closing time.
items.q: What time does Sky Tower close?
items.ex: エレベーターは閉館30分前の9時30分に止まる→閉館は10時。
